subject.title: [Bug]: Non-Anthropic models output tool calls as plain text '[tool: exec]' instead of tool_use blocks

question: When a tool-enabled provider emits only a bare marker such as `[tool: exec]` with no arguments, should OpenClaw retry/fallback/block the turn, warn the operator, or attempt a model-specific recovery path?
rationale: The current parser cannot safely execute a marker without arguments, and the viable fixes change provider fallback, retry, and user-visible failure policy rather than being a narrow parser bug.

options.title: Retry or fall back with a clear diagnostic
options.body: Treat bare markers as failed tool-intent evidence, avoid executing them, and retry or move to a known tool-capable fallback with an operator-visible reason.

options.title: Keep current parser behavior and document limits
options.body: Continue promoting only argument-bearing serialized text calls, and document affected non-native models as manual or text-only for tool-heavy agents.

options.title: Add model-specific prompt or schema pressure controls
options.body: Tune MiniMax/DeepSeek-style routes to reduce marker leakage, but require live proof that the workaround improves tool-heavy turns without breaking native providers.

recommendation.title: Retry or fall back with a clear diagnostic
recommendation.body: Treat bare markers as failed tool-intent evidence, avoid executing them, and retry or move to a known tool-capable fallback with an operator-visible reason.

likelyOwner.reason: This is primarily provider/runtime fallback policy, and recent history ties this owner to adjacent runtime, SDK, and tool-call failure policy changes.
